name: PyTorch 2.15.0 Release
body:
# PyTorch 2.15.0 Release Notes - [Highlights](#highlights) - [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes) - [Deprecations](#deprecations) - [New Features](#new-features) - [Improvements](#improvements) - [Bug fixes](#bug-fixes) - [Performance](#performance) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Security](#security) - [Developers](#developers) # Highlights
Rewritten NCCL backend becomes the default, with a flight recorder that dumps on hangs and TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or nccl-legacy as rollback paths
One-sided transports for torch.distributed, with a NIXL backend and CUDA-graph-capturable transfers
FSDP2 and pipelining gain finer memory and communication control, with fp32 for precision-sensitive parameters, CUDA-graph-captured gradient accumulation, and gradient reduction overlapped with compute
Faster 4-bit (NVFP4) LLM decoding on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs through fewer, better-overlapped kernel launches in NVGEMM
Apple Silicon gains FP8 and faster decode, with float8_e4m3fn and _scaled_mm, a new grouped_mm with a decode fast path (1.32–1.34x tokens/s on MoE decode), and public torch.mps.Stream APIs
Broader platform support with FlyDSL kernels on AMD gfx950, Tensor Data Mover support for gfx1250 (MI450), ROCm 10.0 wheels, simpler SYCL kernel authoring and multi-GPU profiling on Intel GPUs, CUDA 13.2 as the default wheel with CUDA 13.4 alongside it, and torch.compile on Python 3.15
For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release. # Backwards Incompatible Changes ## Python Frontend ### `import torch` can no longer be re-executed in the same process, including via `importlib.reload(torch)` (#194654) `importlib.reload(torch)` and `del sys.modules["torch"]` + re-import now raise, as does retrying `import torch` after it failed. Re-running the module body was already unsafe in exactly the same way as the retry, so the new check does not distinguish the two. Normal use is unaffected: a successful import leaves `torch` in `sys.modules` so the body never re-runs, and re-entrant imports from a backend extension during autoload still short-circuit on `sys.modules` without reaching the check. Version 2.14: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # RuntimeError: Only a single TORCH_LIBRARY can be used to register the namespace triton; ... # (re-importing after a failed `import torch` failed with similarly misleading errors or could segfault) ``` Version 2.15: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # ImportError: `torch` can only be initialized once per process, so this module cannot # be imported again: neither via `importlib.reload(torch)`, nor by re-importing after # a failed `import torch`. ``` ### Nested tensors are no longer allowlisted for `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` (#194380) Nested jagged and strided nested tensors are no longer on the default `weights_only` allowlist. Loading a checkpoint that contains one with `weights_only=True` (the default) now fails with `Unsupported global: GLOBAL torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor._rebuild_njt was not an allowed global by default` (or `GLOBAL torch._utils._rebuild_nested_tensor` for strided nested tensors). To load checkpoints containing nested tensors, allow them explicitly with `torch.serialization.safe_globals` (see below), or use `weights_only=False` for trusted files. Version 2.14: ```python loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) # works ``` Version 2.15: ```python from torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor import _rebuild_njt, NestedTensor with torch.serialization.safe_globals([_rebuild_njt, NestedTensor]): loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) ``` ### Operators called through `torch.ops.*` and `torch._C._dispatch_call_boxed` now use PyTorch's own warning and exception translation instead of pybind11's (#193451) We make `torch.ops.*` calls go through the same exception and warning translation as the rest of the library. This means that some exception translation that used to be handled by pybind is now handled natively. User-defined pybind exception translation is thus lost. Restoring it may be done in a future release as part of a broader exception handler improvement. In addition, `TORCH_WARN` warnings from these operators now reach Python's `warnings` module, so they raise when warnings are turned into errors (`-W error`). `std::out_of_range` still becomes `IndexError` (#195713). Version 2.14: ```python # C++ op: throw std::invalid_argument("bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: # pybind11 translation ... ``` Version 2.15: ```python # C++ op: TORCH_CHECK_VALUE(false, "bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: ... # TORCH_WARN from the op is now a Python warning with warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter("ignore") torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) ``` ## Autograd ### Selective activation checkpointing now saves, rather than recomputes, the outputs of operators with an ordered effect unless the policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` (#196956) In eager mode, if a `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts` policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE` for a non-aliasing operator with an ordered effect (e.g. via `register_effect(torch.library.EffectType.ORDERED)`), that choice is now overridden and its outputs are saved, so the side effect is no longer replayed during backward. This can increase activation memory. To keep the 2.14 behavior, return `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` for that operator. Operators in the `c10d` namespace are excluded. Under `torch.compile`, `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` on an effectful operator now raises at compile time: `RuntimeError: AOTAutograd does not support MUST_RECOMPUTE for effectful operations because forward effects cannot join the backward effect-token chain.` Use a save policy instead. ```python policy = lambda ctx, op, *args, **kwargs: CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE checkpoint(fn, x, use_reentrant=False, context_fn=lambda: create_selective_checkpoint_contexts(policy)) # 2.14: an effectful op in fn runs twice; 2.15: once (use CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE to replay) ``` ## Distributed (c10d) ### The `nccl` backend now uses a rewritten, cleaned-up NCCL implementation by default (#192281, #192895, #193237, #193241) `backend="nccl"` (also the default CUDA backend of `init_process_group()`) now creates the new implementation. The legacy implementation is available as `backend="nccl-legacy"` for this release only: **`nccl-legacy` and `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` will be removed in the next release**, so migrate to `nccl` or `nccl-lazy`. Use `nccl` (eager initialization) by default. Use `nccl-lazy` when you need independent point-to-point communicators: collectives run on one eagerly created communicator, and each send/recv peer pair gets its own lazily created communicator and stream, so concurrent P2P to different peers can overlap (as in the legacy backend). Differences from the legacy backend: - Communicators are created eagerly in `init_process_group()`/`new_group()`, allocating GPU memory even for unused groups. - Each group is bound to one CUDA device: `device_id`, else `LOCAL_RANK % torch.cuda.device_count()` (or the global rank modulo the device count); `torch.cuda.set_device()` is not used. Tensors on another GPU fail with `Expected tensor on cuda:X but found tensor on cuda:Y` or `ProcessGroupNCCL is bound to device cuda:X but an operation was issued on cuda:Y`. Pass `device_id` if needed; several GPUs per process requires `nccl-legacy`. - `dist.get_backend_impl(...)` returns the new backend class, so `isinstance(..., ProcessGroupNCCL)` is `False` and legacy-only methods such as `comm_split_count()` are missing. - An async `all_gather`'s `work.get_future()` value is the list of per-rank outputs, not a one-element list holding a stacked tensor; read the output list passed to `all_gather` instead (works on both backends). To temporarily restore the legacy behavior in 2.15, set `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` on every rank before creating the process group, or use `nccl-legacy`: Version 2.14: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl") # ProcessGroupNCCL ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # new implementation dist.init_process_group("nccl-lazy", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # independent P2P communicators dist.init_process_group("nccl-legacy") # legacy implementation, removed in the next release ``` ## Distributed Checkpointing ### Distributed checkpoint metadata now records tensor strides, so checkpoints saved with PyTorch 2.15 cannot be loaded by PyTorch 2.14 or earlier (#194251) `TensorProperties` gains an optional `strides` field in the pickled `.metadata` file. In older versions `dcp.load` raises a `CheckpointException` reporting `too many values to unpack (expected 5)`. There is no flag to write the old format. Version 2.14 (loading a 2.15 checkpoint): ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # CheckpointException: ... too many values to unpack (expected 5) ``` Version 2.15: ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # loads 2.14 and 2.15 checkpoints ``` ## Distributed FSDP2 ### With `MixedPrecisionPolicy(reduce_dtype=None)`, `fully_shard` now accumulates and reduces gradients in the parameter's `grad_dtype` (its original dtype by default) instead of in `param_dtype` (#194434) **This is BC-breaking**: `mp_policy.reduce_dtype=None` no longer defaults to `mp_policy.param_dtype`. * [popular case] fp32 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=bf16)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 (2x reduce-scatter bytes) * [rare case] bf16 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=fp32)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 How to deal with BC: explicitly set `mp_policy.reduce_dtype`. In grad accumulation (no reduce-scatter), the unsharded param's `.grad` always holds the accumulated value, visible via `model.parameters()` while unsharded. Before this change, `.grad` was `None` when `reduce_dtype` was set and differed from `param_dtype` (FSDP kept the sum in a hidden `reduce_dtype` buffer). Version 2.14: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in bf16 ``` Version 2.15: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in fp32 # to keep the 2.14 behavior, set reduce_dtype explicitly mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16, reduce_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) ``` ## Distributed Pipelining ### `torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p` is renamed to `pipeline_per_edge_p2p` and now uses one communicator per directed rank-to-rank edge (#196666) The old names were removed with no alias: setting the attribute raises `AttributeError: torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p does not exist`, and `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_DIRECTION_P2P` is silently ignored. Version 2.14: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_edge_p2p = True # or TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_EDGE_P2P=1 ``` ## Profiler ### C++ stack traces are now symbolized with `dladdr` instead of `addr2line` by default (#195462) `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE` now defaults to on, since `addr2line` is slow and can hang. C++ frames in `TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1` errors and CUDA memory snapshots now show the library path and offset, plus the symbol name only if exported (otherwise `??`). To restore `addr2line`, set `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0` or `TORCH_SYMBOLIZE_MODE=addr2line`. ```bash TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1 TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0 python train.py ``` ### CUDA memory snapshots record the allocator's `mallocWithAddress` tag in a new `internal_metadata` field instead of appending it to `user_metadata` (#193432) `user_metadata` in `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` trace entries is now exactly what was set with `torch.cuda.memory._set_memory_metadata` (which now also accepts a dict). Tools that searched `user_metadata` for `mallocWithAddress` must read `internal_metadata` instead. ```python # 2.14 tagged = [e for e in trace if "mallocWithAddress" in e["user_metadata"]] # 2.15 tagged = [e for e in trace if e.get("internal_metadata") == "mallocWithAddress"] ``` ### Remove the deprecated `FunctionEvent.metadata_json` property (#198265) Accessing it now raises `AttributeError: 'FunctionEvent' object has no attribute 'metadata_json'`, and the `metadata_json` constructor argument is removed. Use `FunctionEvent.metadata`, a dict populated when `_ExperimentalConfig(expose_kineto_event_metadata=True)` is set (not the deprecated `event_metadata`). ```python metadata = event.metadata_json # 2.14: JSON string metadata = event.metadata # 2.15: dict[str, Any] or None ``` ### Rename the experimental CUPTI monitor profiler backend to Cuspy, without aliases for the old names (#195881) In `_ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config=...)`, `"cupti_monitor"` is now `"cuspy"` and `"cupti_monitor_async_export"` is now `"cuspy_async_export"`; old names silently fall back to the default Kineto backend. `prof.take_pending_cupti_export()` is now `take_pending_cuspy_export()` (the old name raises `AttributeError`). Prefer the new `torch.profiler.CuspyConfig`. ```python # 2.14 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cupti_monitor"}') # 2.15 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cuspy"}') ``` ## Dynamo ### Higher-order ops now reject input mutation and aliasing in their bodies unless the op opts in (#185738) Before, Dynamo let any higher-order op body mutate or alias its inputs by default. Ops that do not implement those semantics could silently produce invalid graphs. Mutation and aliasing are now off by default. The built-in wrappers that support them (`wrap`, checkpoint, `autograd.Function`, autocast/set-grad wrappers) opt in. A `flex_attention` `mask_mod` may read captured views but must not mutate inputs or return aliases. Under `fullgraph=True`, unsupported mutation or aliasing raises `Encountered input mutation during higher order op tracing` or `Encountered aliasing during higher order op tracing`; otherwise, Dynamo graph breaks and falls back to eager execution. Rewrite the higher-order op body to avoid mutation or aliasing. For example, rewrite an in-place `flex_attention` score modifier as an out-of-place operation: Version 2.14: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): score.add_(1) return score.clone() ``` Version 2.15: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): return score + 1 ``` ## Inductor ### `torch.compiler.nested_compile_region(options=...)` now accepts only an allowlist of Inductor config patches (#195864, #195865) Patches passed through `get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches=..., bw_inductor_config_patches=...)` used to accept any `torch._inductor.config` key, though many were silently ignored. Only `fallback_by_default` and `max_autotune` are now accepted; other keys raise `ValueError: Inductor config key '' is not supported in forward nested compile-region options` (or `backward`). Apply other options to the whole compiled function. Patch dictionaries are now snapshotted when the options are created, so later mutation has no effect, and the default no longer implicitly sets `triton.autotune_at_compile_time=True`. Version 2.14: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` Version 2.15: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"max_autotune": True}) compiled = torch.compile(fn, options={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` ### `torch.compiler.precompile` is now a module instead of a callable; capture with `torch.compiler.precompile.capture(...)` and reload with `torch.compiler.precompile.load(...)` (#197993, #198135, #198213) Calling `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` now raises `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable`. `capture(fn, *, artifact_path, cache_path)` returns a context manager that you call once inside the `with` block; it writes both files when the block exits cleanly (or on `cap.save()`), and `load` now takes those paths. `decompositions=` moves to `tracer=MakeFxTracer(decompositions=...)`. Version 2.14: ```python python_code, cache = torch.compiler.precompile(lambda m, x: m(x), model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load(python_code, cache) ``` Version 2.15: ```python with torch.compiler.precompile.capture(lambda m, x: m(x), artifact_path="m.py", cache_path="m.cache") as cap: cap(model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache") ``` ## Composability ### Under functionalization, a regenerated output of `split`, `split_with_sizes` or `unbind` is now rebuilt as a single `slice` or `select` of its base, so its `grad_fn` is `SliceBackward0`/`SelectBackward0` instead of `SplitBackward0`/`SplitWithSizesBackward0`/`UnbindBackward0` (#194037) This greatly reduces compile time for code that mutates many `split()` views (for example 32s to 15s with 128 views). Gradients are unchanged, but the in-place error now names the new op with output index 0: `RuntimeError: Output 0 of Select is a view and is being modified inplace.` Code that inspects `grad_fn` names, matches the old error text, or pattern-matches `split`/`unbind` nodes in functionalized graphs needs updating. There is no option to restore the previous behavior. Version 2.14: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) # f returns base.unbind(0)[1] after base.add_(1) >>> out.grad_fn ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) >>> out.grad_fn ``` ## Release Engineering ### PyPI wheels now ship with CUDA 13.2, and CUDA 12.6 and CUDA 13.0 wheels are no longer published (#196249, #198913) The default PyPI wheel moves from CUDA 13.0 to CUDA 13.2. The 2.15 wheels are `cu132` and `cu134`; `cu126` and `cu130` are no longer built. CUDA 13 wheels need NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and a GPU of Turing (`sm_75`) or newer, so Maxwell, Pascal and Volta GPUs and hosts with a CUDA 12.x driver should stay on 2.14. Version 2.15: ```bash # PyPI wheel now uses CUDA 13.2 pip install torch # CUDA 13.4 wheels pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu134 # To stay on CUDA 12.6 or CUDA 13.0, pin PyTorch 2.14: pip install torch==2.14.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126 # or cu130 ``` ### Python 3.10 wheels are no longer published (#198233, #199398) PyTorch 2.15 raises the minimum supported Python version for binaries to 3.11: no `cp310` wheels are built for `torch` or the Triton wheels, and CI no longer tests on Python 3.10. On Python 3.10, `pip` cannot find a 2.15 wheel. Upgrade to Python 3.11 or newer, or stay on PyTorch 2.14. Version 2.14: ```bash python3.10 -m pip install torch # cp310 wheel available ``` Version 2.15: ```bash python3.11 -m pip install torch==2.15.0 # Python 3.11 through 3.15 (including 3.14t and 3.15t) ``` ### ROCm wheels move to ROCm 7.14 and 10.0; ROCm 7.2 wheels and gfx900/gfx906 kernels are dropped (#194919) gfx900 (MI25) and gfx906 (MI50/MI60, Radeon VII) users can stay on 2.14 (`rocm7.2`) or build from source with those targets in `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH`. ```bash pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.14 # or rocm10.0 ``` ### Linux CUDA wheels no longer depend on the cuRAND library (#194850) PyTorch only uses the cuRAND device API, so `torch` no longer links `libcurand`, no longer preloads it on `import torch`, and the wheel's CUDA requirements no longer include cuRAND. Extensions or libraries that call the cuRAND host API (for example `curandCreateGenerator`) and relied on `pip install torch` bringing in the cuRAND library can fail to load `libcurand.so` and must now install it themselves. Version 2.15: ```bash pip install torch pip install "cuda-toolkit[curand]==13.2.2" # match the toolkit version of your wheel ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.histc(..., out=...)` on CUDA now raises an error when `out` does not have the same dtype as the input (#196100) CUDA used to silently cast into any `out` dtype. It now matches CPU and MPS and rejects mismatches, even widening ones. Compute without `out` and cast instead. Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0, out=int64_out) # silently truncated ``` Version 2.15: ```python RuntimeError: torch.histogram: input tensor and hist tensor should have the same dtype, but got input float and hist long int >>> int64_out.copy_(torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0)) # workaround ``` ### On CUDA, cuBLAS and cuBLASLt workspaces are now allocated for each operation instead of being cached per handle and stream (#194311) Graphs captured separately on one stream could share the cached workspace and fail on replay with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Workspaces are now freed after each op, so `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` excludes them and the handle from `torch.cuda.current_blas_handle()` has no ATen workspace attached. Set `TORCH_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CACHE=1` to restore caching (unsafe with multiple graphs on one stream). `TORCH_CUBLASLT_UNIFIED_WORKSPACE` now only takes effect with caching enabled. ROCm has a matching change (#196920). Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.mm(a, a, out=out) >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before > 0 # workspace stays allocated True ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before # freed after the op 0 ``` ## CPU (AArch64) ### Float32 `torch.sin` and `torch.cos` on Arm CPUs (NEON and SVE) now use SLEEF's 3.5-ULP kernels instead of the 1.0-ULP kernels, matching the accuracy of the x86 AVX2 implementation and running 1.7x-2.4x faster on Neoverse V1/V2 (#196315) Float32 `sin` and `cos` results on Arm can now differ from earlier releases in the last bits. Bit-for-bit comparisons against stored golden outputs, `torch.equal`, or `torch.testing.assert_close` with `rtol=0, atol=0` may fail; default `assert_close` tolerances are unaffected. There is no switch to restore the previous kernels; if you need tighter accuracy, compute in float64 and cast back. Version 2.14: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 1 ULP ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 2 ULP >>> x.double().cos().float() # workaround: correctly rounded ``` ## MPS ### The MPS backend now requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer (#199261, #200290) macOS 14 has reached end of life, so its MPS workarounds were removed. On macOS 14, `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` returns `False` and allocating on `mps` raises the error below. To keep using MPS, stay on PyTorch 2.14 or upgrade macOS; CPU builds still run on older macOS. C++ extensions: `at::mps::MacOSVersion::MACOS_14_4` was removed. ```python >>> torch.ones(2, device="mps") # 2.15 on macOS 14 RuntimeError: The MPS backend is supported on macOS 15.0+. Current OS version can be queried using `sw_vers` ``` ## XPU ### Remove the `allocator` property from `torch.xpu.MemPool`, aligning with other accelerators (#192041) `torch.xpu.MemPool` no longer exposes the allocator it was constructed with, so `pool.allocator` now raises `AttributeError`. Keep your own reference to the allocator instead; passing one to the `MemPool` constructor is unchanged. Before: ```python pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(allocator.allocator()) my_allocator = pool.allocator ``` After: ```python my_allocator = allocator.allocator() pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(my_allocator) ``` ## Complex Frontend ### Ops that are undefined for complex inputs now raise `TypeError` instead of `RuntimeError` (#192350) This covers order-dependent ops (`sort`, `argsort`, `topk`, `argmax`/`argmin`, `max`/`min` with `dim`, `maximum`/`minimum`, `fmax`/`fmin`, `aminmax`), `isposinf`/`isneginf`, `view_as_real`/`imag` on real tensors, and `view_as_complex` on complex tensors, matching Python (`1j < 2j` is a `TypeError`). `except RuntimeError:` no longer catches these; catch `(RuntimeError, TypeError)`. Ops not yet implemented for a dtype (e.g. `rad2deg`, `nansum`, `heaviside` on complex, `topk`/`argmax` on bool) now raise `NotImplementedError`, which `except RuntimeError:` still catches. Full `max()`/`min()`/`amax`/`amin` are unchanged. ```python torch.sort(torch.randn(3, dtype=torch.cfloat)) # 2.14: RuntimeError: Sort does not support complex dtypes on CPU # 2.15: TypeError: Sort does not support complex dtypes on CPU ``` # Deprecations ## Optimizer ### Passing a bare `set` of parameters to an optimizer is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning`; it will become an error in a future release (#198710) Set iteration order can change between runs, so optimizer state could silently mismatch parameters on reload. The warning reads: `optimizer parameters need to be organized in ordered collections, but the ordering of tensors in sets will change between runs. Please use a list instead.` ```python opt = torch.optim.Adam(set(model.parameters())) # 2.15: FutureWarning opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(model.parameters())) # recommended ``` ## Linear Algebra Frontend ### MAGMA is deprecated for LU factorization with pivoting on CUDA: `torch.linalg.lu_factor`, `torch.linalg.lu`, and the ops that use it internally (`torch.linalg.solve`, `torch.linalg.inv`, `torch.linalg.det`, `torch.linalg.slogdet`) now always use cuSOLVER (#190661) This only affects code that sets `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("magma")`: pivoted LU now uses cuSOLVER anyway; a new built-in batched LU kernel replaces MAGMA's for large batches. When MAGMA is preferred, the first call warns: `linalg.lu_factor: MAGMA, as a linear algebra backend, is deprecated and will be removed in future releases.` `pivot=False` still uses MAGMA when it is preferred. To avoid the warning, use the default or cuSOLVER backend. ```python torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("magma") LU, pivots = torch.linalg.lu_factor(A) # 2.14: MAGMA; 2.15: cuSOLVER + UserWarning torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("default") # recommended ``` ## Profiler ### `torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof`, `parse_nvprof_trace` and `EnforceUnique` are deprecated and will be removed in PyTorch 2.17 (#198396) `nvprof` does not support recent GPUs. They now emit a `FutureWarning` such as `` `torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof` is deprecated and will be removed in PyTorch 2.17. `` Use `torch.profiler.profile` or Nsight Systems with `torch.autograd.profiler.emit_nvtx()`. ```python events = torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof("trace.prof") # 2.14 with torch.profiler.profile() as prof: # 2.15 run_workload() ``` ### `FunctionEvent.event_metadata` is deprecated in favor of `FunctionEvent.metadata` (#198405) `metadata` is a typed `dict[str, Any]` with everything `event_metadata` had. Accessing `event_metadata` emits `FutureWarning: `event_metadata` is deprecated. Use `metadata` instead.` ```python grid = event.event_metadata.grid # 2.14 grid = event.metadata["grid"] # 2.15 ``` ## Inductor ### Deprecate `torch._inductor.config.triton.use_block_ptr` because Triton removed its block-pointer API (#191007) With a Triton that no longer provides block pointers, `use_block_ptr=True` is now a no-op that falls back to the default indexing path with a one-time `FutureWarning: config.triton.use_block_ptr=True but the installed Triton no longer provides the block-pointer frontend API`, instead of failing with `CompilationError: ... Block pointers have been removed in favor of the tensor descriptor API`. Use tensor descriptors instead. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.triton.use_block_ptr = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python torch._inductor.config.triton.use_tensor_descriptor = True ``` ### Deprecate the no-op `torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm` and `torch._inductor.config.mixed_mm_choice` settings (#193721) These settings have been ignored since the tuned `mixed_mm` path was removed. Reading or setting either now emits a one-time `FutureWarning` such as `torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm is deprecated and does not do anything`. `autoheuristic_collect.mixed_mm` and `autoheuristic_use.mixed_mm` were removed, and `"mixed_mm"` is no longer the `TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOHEURISTIC_USE` default. Delete these settings from your code. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm = True # silently ignored ``` Version 2.15: ```python # FutureWarning; delete the line ``` ### Rename `torch._inductor.config.benchmark_epilogue_fusion` to `benchmark_template_fusion` and `max_epilogue_benchmarked_choices` to `max_template_fusion_benchmarked_choices` (#198430) The settings also cover prologue fusion, so the old names were misleading. The old names remain as deprecated aliases that emit a one-time `FutureWarning`. The environment variable is now `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_TEMPLATE_FUSION`; `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_EPILOGUE_FUSION` is still read as a fallback. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.benchmark_epilogue_fusion = False ``` Version 2.15: ```python torch._inductor.config.benchmark_template_fusion = False ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.cuda.graph_annotations.clear_kernel_annotations()` is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning` (#195398) The CUDA graph kernel annotation registry now cleans up after itself: annotations are rekeyed to the executable graph when it is instantiated and dropped when that graph is destroyed. A global clear also discards annotations for graphs that are still live. Remove the call, and reset or delete a graph to drop its annotations. Version 2.14: ```python annotations = get_kernel_annotations() clear_kernel_annotations() ``` Version 2.15: ```python annotations = get_kernel_annotations() # No clear needed; g's annotations are dropped when g is reset or destroyed. ``` # New Features ## torch.nn - Add `torch.nn.functional.scaled_addmm` and in-place `scaled_addmm_`, which compute `beta * input + alpha * scaled_mm(mat1, mat2)` in a single cuBLASLt GEMM on CUDA with the same scaling recipes as `scaled_mm`; also supported under `torch.compile` (#195409, #195410) ## Optimizer - Add `torch.optim.functional`, a public module of functional optimizers (`adam`, `adamw`, `sgd`, `muon` and others) that run the same implementations as the optimizer classes while the caller manages parameters, gradients and state (#194986) ## Autograd - Add `ctx.input_grad_buffers` to custom `torch.autograd.Function` backward, exposing the engine's gradient accumulation buffers (or `None` when unavailable) so a fused kernel can accumulate an input's gradient in place and return `None` for it. Availability depends on backward order, so keep an out-of-place fallback; buffers must be updated synchronously within the current `backward` call, and the property is unavailable with `create_graph=True`, anomaly detection, or post-hooks on the producing node (#196491) - Add `torch.autograd.graph.queue_callback(callback)`, a public API to run a callback when the current backward pass finishes (#193958) ## Distributed (c10d) - Add an experimental one-sided transport API, `torch.distributed._transport`, with a NIXL backend and CUDA-graph-capturable stream-ordered transfers (#195643, #197032, #198889, #198918) - Add an experimental pure-Python watchdog, `torch.distributed._watchdog`, that detects hung CPU and GPU operations in Python distributed backends and dumps thread stacks on timeout (#192075) - Add `get_peer_cft_handle(peer)` and `get_multimem_cft_handle()` to NCCL symmetric memory for NCCL Compute Fabric Transport (#191685) - Add `ProcessGroupNCCL.Options.lazy_init` so `nccl` and `nccl-lazy` groups create their communicator on first use instead of allocating ~200 MiB in `new_group` (#200020) ## Distributed Checkpointing - `FsspecReader` and `FsspecWriter` are now public in `torch.distributed.checkpoint`, and `FsspecWriter` supports `dcp.async_save` through a new `cache_staged_state_dict` argument placed before `overwrite` (pass `overwrite` and later arguments by keyword); importing the old private `_fsspec_filesystem` module emits a `DeprecationWarning` (#188698) ## Distributed FSDP2 - Add `FSDPModule.set_manual_backward_finalization(True)` and `FSDPModule.finalize_backward()` to run gradient reduction and resharding at a chosen point instead of in the autograd final callback (#196640) - Add `finalize_backward(async_op=True)`, which returns a `GradientReductionHandle` so gradient reduction can overlap other compute (#196724) - Add `FSDPModule.set_keep_unsharded_storage()` to keep unsharded parameter storage allocated across `reshard()` (#198417) - Let tensor-subclass parameters free raw all-gather buffers right after `fsdp_post_all_gather` by implementing `fsdp_should_release_all_gather_outputs_after_post_all_gather()` (#194114) ## Distributed Pipelining - Add `PipelineStage.register_forward_context(factory)` to wrap each stage forward in a context manager that receives the stage and microbatch indices (#196462) - Add `torch.distributed.pipelining.analyze_pipeline_activation_liveness`, which computes activation lifetimes and reusable storage slots from a schedule (#196464) ## DeviceMesh - Add the experimental `DeviceMesh.abort()` to abort all process groups of a root mesh, avoiding hangs when a peer exits early (#189655) ## Profiler - Add `torch.profiler.ProfilerActivityConfig` and `torch.profiler.PerformanceMetricsConfig` to configure collection per activity group, such as CUDA hardware performance counters (#196065) - Fix MPS `scaled_dot_product_attention` output shape with broadcast batch/head dims, and `scatter_add_`/`index_add_` on offset `bool` views (#189631, #195081) - Raise errors for MPS command buffer failures (such as out of memory) and MPS-to-CPU copies to `float64` instead of returning wrong outputs (#198883, #197722) - Fix crashes and hangs when running MPS ops from multiple threads, and hangs in MPS event `elapsed_time()` (#167541, #197836, #196395) - Fix DLPack export of sliced MPS tensors, Metal debug-layer validation failures, and `active_bytes` in MPS memory stats (#182924, #199452, #193838) - Fix `torch.linalg.svd` returning non-orthonormal `U`/`Vh` with `full_matrices=True`, inaccurate results for very small or large entries, and zero `pinv`/`lstsq` for small singular values (#200536, #200776, #200649) - Fix complex division (and complex `linalg.solve`, `solve_triangular`, `det`) returning NaN or 0 for extreme magnitudes, and complex `pow` returning 0 for every zero base (#200765, #200564) - Fix `var`/`std` returning 0 instead of NaN for NaN/Inf inputs, `float16` `addmm` overflowing to `inf` with `beta=0`, and `grouped_mm` silently accepting mismatched dtypes (#200758, #200657, #200659) - Fix `torch.compile` truncating `int64` constants to 32 bits (#201060) ## ROCm - Fix flash and memory-efficient attention failing on empty inputs; they now return empty outputs like CUDA (#195812, #195813, #196723, #198022) - Fix CK flash attention dropout returning a wrong seed/offset to autograd when the GPU is busy (#197563) - Fix incorrect SDPA results on gfx11 with AOTriton 0.11 and later (#194280) - Fix launch failures on large inputs in `pdist`/`cdist` (#188006) and the BMM outer-product kernel (#194131) - Fix FP8 GEMMs failing with `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` on ROCm 7.14 (#197201) - Fix crashes and hangs when a captured backward pass creates a hipBLASLt handle during CUDA graph capture (#196399) - Fix incorrect Inductor BF16 atomic accumulation, e.g. `index_put_` with repeated indices, on gfx11/gfx12 (#198199) - Fix nondeterministic `torch.topk` output order on slices longer than 256 elements (#199425) - Fix `F.batch_norm` on sharded DTensor inputs (#197160) - Fix hipify narrowing 64-bit and unsigned `std::max`/`std::min` arguments to `int` (#199444) - Fix JIT C++ extensions failing with `hipblas/hipblas.h: No such file or directory` with ROCm from TheRock pip wheels (#196503) - Stop RCCL 2.28+ from printing a deprecation warning on every all-to-all (#197534, #199124) - Fix rare incorrect indices from `argmax`, `argmin`, `max` and `min` for large reductions on ROCm (#193291) ## XPU - Fix wrong `conv1d` backward results on XPU for some singleton-dimension layouts, caused by detecting the memory format before the 3D-to-4D view used by the oneDNN path (#194328) - Fix batch norm accuracy, `fft`/`ifft` on empty batches, `norm` global reductions, and half-precision `sampled_addmm` on XPU (#193929) - Fix precision loss in `addmm` and `baddbmm` for bf16/fp16 with non-trivial `alpha`/`beta` on XPU, which now accumulate in fp32 as CPU and CUDA do (#174864) - Fix `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` under-reporting free memory on Xe2 and later GPUs (#195987) - Fix XPU device indices not matching SYCL's order on platforms that enumerate an integrated GPU before the discrete ones (#198336) - Fix oneDNN SDPA with grouped-query attention and a mask broadcast in the head dimension (#194973) - Fix `torch.xpu.Event.record()` enqueueing two commands on first use, which could leave the event without profiling data and intermittently fail Inductor autotuning (#194609) - Fix "An event cannot be enqueued for signaling or waiting behind a command which is not enqueued in the backend" errors with oneCCL on Intel® Arc™ B-Series Graphics, by limiting reusable events to the IPC case (#197396) - Fix `_safe_softmax` incorrectly zeroing rows that contain NaN on XPU (#195708) - Fix incorrect `_weight_int4pack_mm` results on XPU (#195708) - Fix undefined behavior with NaN inputs in `topk`, a spurious `group_reduce` assert, and fused moving-average observer/fake-quantize dtype mismatches on XPU (#194185) - Fix an abort in the XPU flash attention backward with an empty batch, and return BSHD-contiguous input gradients from the XPU efficient attention backward (#198200) - Fix `weight_norm` running out of memory for 1-D inputs on XPU, and a host-to-device metadata race in nested `_transform_bias_rescale_qkv` (#200289) - Fix RNG stream reuse for large tensors on XPU (#200289) - Fix Inductor treating every XPU kernel that uses scratch memory as spilling registers (#197061) ## Complex Frontend - Fix `F.dropout` raising `NotImplementedError` for complex inputs (#195373) ## JIT - Fix `torch.jit.Attribute` and `nn.Module` class annotations being lost on Python 3.14; this requires `typing-extensions>=4.13` (#195201, #199074) - Fix constant pooling merging `0.0` with `-0.0` (#192605) - Fix `torch.jit.export_opnames` missing ops inside `torch.jit.fork` subgraphs (#197333) ## Mobile - Fix a race in `CPUCachingAllocator` teardown (#196759) ## Sparse Frontend - Fix concurrent `torch.load` calls interfering in sparse tensor validation (#194751) - Fix wrong values from sparse compressed `add` with `out=` and ROCm COO `coalesce` (#197564, #199484) - Fix semi-structured bitmask conversion on non-CUDA devices (#193943) ## torch.func - Fix `torch.vmap` falling back to the slow loop for several loss ops and `addr` under `python -O` (#192859) # Performance ## Python Frontend - Reduce `TensorIterator` overhead and dtype refcount contention under free-threading (#194422, #194371) ## torch.nn - Speed up `nn.Module.__call__` by about 15% (#196236) - Add a channels-last CUDA `GroupNorm` kernel (#191945) - Speed up RMSNorm backward up to 2x on sm12x and chunked `linear_cross_entropy` by 6-10% (#192400, #196134) ## Distributed (c10d) - Speed up `all_gather_object` (#196185) - Share the parent `Store` connection across `split_group` child groups (#196665) - Use the NVLS multicast (multimem) barrier for CUDA symmetric memory when a multicast mapping is available (#192861) ## DistributedDataParallel (DDP) - Batch DDP's copy into `.grad` with `batched_grad_copy=True` (#190524) ## Distributed FSDP2 - Reduce reduce-scatter gradient memory for size-1 shard groups and low-precision gradients (#196348, #198668) ## Distributed Pipelining - Lower peak memory and improve overlap via lazy receive buffers and new `defer_reduce_grad_wait`/`unshard_lookahead` options (#196463, #196963, #196725, #196706) ## Linear Algebra Frontend - Add a built-in CUDA batched LU kernel that matches MAGMA, and improve LU backend selection without pivoting (#190329, #193004) ## FX - Reduce compile time in FX `from_node` provenance tracking (#193051) - Speed up the FX accelerator splitter on large graphs (#198519, #198654) ## Dynamo - Reduce per-call overhead of compiled code and helpers like `assert_size_stride` (#190623, #195951, #198019, #196771, #197451, #197733) - Reduce compile time: defer gen-2 GC while compiling (4.2s on one model; see `gc_gen2_threshold_during_compile`), skip empty graphs (custom backends are no longer called for such graphs), and speed up large functions (#193289, #193157, #195622) ## Inductor - Reduce compile time by caching in fusion search and codegen, hashing sources in the background, and compiling combo-kernel benchmarks in parallel (#186319, #192817, #192820, #194010, #194011, #198747, #198881, #198320) - Allow mix-order reduction fusion for more shapes, speeding up RMSNorm backward (#186370, #188660) - Reduce `cpp_wrapper` kernel call overhead by 40-50% (#192287) - Improve CPU FlexAttention BF16 performance by 6-29% (#191780) - Use larger reduction tiles on GB300, roughly doubling HBM bandwidth use (#193774) - Add gfx950 FlexAttention backward configs (1.8-2.3x faster) (#194151) - Improve NVGEMM NVFP4 decode performance on Blackwell and widen its autotuning candidates (#194651, #194652, #197485, #195539, #198293) - Compute only one triangle for large BF16 `X @ X.T` on SM100 (#194177, #194178) - Speed up collective bucketing, including up to 9x faster uneven reduce-scatter padding (#196647, #196621, #195616) - Simplify `slice_scatter` chains to reduce recomputation and peak memory (#192136, #195608, #195631) - Fix CPU OpenMP parallelization moving onto inner reduction loops under freezing, and recover an XPU inner-reduction regression (#190928, #190986) - Fuse `torch.cat`/`torch.stack` copies into foreach kernels for dynamic shapes (#198294) - Enable nested reduction fusion by default (`TORCHINDUCTOR_NESTED_REDUCTION=0` disables it), fusing patterns such as RMSNorm followed by MXFP8/NVFP4 quantization into one kernel (#190594, #190595, #191974, #193598, #196332, #196333, #196334) ## Ahead-Of-Time Inductor (AOTI) - Parallelize pinned host staging copies when loading CUDA constants (#195257) ## AOTDispatcher - Speed up the min-cut partitioner, reducing cold compile time by about 5% (#197724) ## Composability - Speed up FakeTensor view cache hits (#192821) - Reduce compile time in `ShapeEnv` (#193219, #193161, #195623) ## Quantization - Speed up AArch64 small-batch QNNPACK linear 2-4x (#193595) ## Foreach - Reduce `_foreach_norm`/`max` CUDA scratch memory (#190549) ## CUDA - Avoid CPU-GPU synchronization when assigning scalars through indexing on CUDA, e.g. `x[mask] = 1.0` (#189303, #188330, #198811) - Speed up CUDA `upsample_linear1d` by 5-25x for small outputs (#180885), pooling backward (#191086, #195119, #196156), dtype-conversion copies (#195542, #198723), 2D transpose copies (#194310), and `zero_` (#195303, #198565) - `torch.topk` on CUDA 13 Linux wheels uses ahead-of-time compiled radix-select kernels on Hopper and Blackwell (median 2.16x on H100) (#190899) - Fix a 10-30x slowdown of `gather`, `index_select`, `x[idx]` and `scatter_add` on rows of 16 or 32 bytes (#200995) ## cuDNN - Prefer the cuDNN backend for SDPA on sm86/sm89 for higher performance (#192799) ## CPU (x86) - Fix the CPU kernel dispatch cache never being populated, which made every dispatch to a CPU kernel repeat the CPU capability selection (#195328) ## CPU (AArch64) - Optimize `libtorch` code layout with LLVM BOLT, using profiles shipped in the repository. The new `USE_LLVM_BOLT` build option is on by default for Linux aarch64 CUDA builds when `llvm-bolt` 21 or newer is found and `USE_PRIORITIZED_TEXT_FOR_LD` is enabled, giving up to 30% faster workloads in some cases and up to 3% slower in others; set `USE_LLVM_BOLT=0` to opt out in source builds (#186245) - Use the native GEMV path for single-column (`n == 1`) BF16 GEMMs on Arm Neoverse CPUs built with oneDNN ACL, for about 5x faster single-thread GPT-2 BF16 decode on Graviton 4 and 5 (1.4x-2.7x with 8-64 threads on Graviton 5) (#198411) - Dispatch non-contiguous FP16 matmuls to oneDNN ACL GEMM kernels instead of the reference implementation on AArch64 (#198498) ## MPS - Move more MPS ops (`softmax`, `nll_loss`, padding, `where`, ...) to native Metal kernels, cutting launch overhead and driver memory growth with variable shapes (#196071, #195441, #195153, #195368, #193826, #198719, #198688, #198497, #196924, #189548, #199687, #198878) - Speed up MPS reductions, linear algebra, GEMV, convolutions, `histc`, masked fill, dropout and sort (#198494, #198611, #198635, #197397, #198646, #199278, #198721, #197862, #196241, #196900, #195944, #198732, #195950, #193623, #193167, #192164, #196016, #195020, #195011, #198960, #196922) - Speed up `softmax` over a non-innermost dim and `relu`, `clamp_min`, `leaky_relu` and other scalar-argument unary ops on row-strided views (#199758, #199933) ## XPU - Speed up SDPA training on XPU by aligning the oneDNN graph SDPA pattern with oneDNN v3.13 and integrating its GQA and dropout support (#195419) - Fuse the `GroupNorm` forward into a single kernel and speed up contiguous `cat` with vectorized stores on XPU (#194842) - Avoid register spilling in mixed fp32/bf16/fp16 elementwise kernels on XPU by adding vectorized type-casting loads (#194185) - Speed up `col2im` on XPU by replacing its hard-coded work-group size (#198720) - Reduce oneMKL LAPACK overhead on XPU by trimming scratchpad initialization, host synchronizations and re-allocation (#193110) ## JIT - Speed up `torch.jit.load` and graph pre-optimization (#194035, #193107, #193250, #194009) # Documentation ## Python Frontend - Document undefined behavior of bool tensors holding bytes other than 0/1, and clarify `Tensor.index_add_`'s `index` argument (#199012, #193403) ## torch.nn - Fix the `linear_cross_entropy` docstring snippet and `nn.RNN` example, and document bias with probability targets (#198941, #188433, #173888) ## Autograd - Document that custom `Function`/op backward gradients may have arbitrary strides and that `unpack_hook` order is unspecified (#195210, #198016) - Point `torch.utils.checkpoint` docs to `torch_remat` and drop the stale `use_reentrant` "version 2.9" error notice (#193998, #193720) - Fix math rendering on the autograd mechanics page (#192562) ## Distributed - Document the remaining NVSHMEM bindings (#193449) ## Distributed (c10d) - Add a tutorial for the distributed debug server (#178800) - Document `Backend.Options` and fix `irecv` and NCCL env var docs (#196123, #189623, #194701) ## Distributed FSDP2 - Document parameter-mutation limits of `fully_shard` (#198826) ## TorchElastic - Fix the `EtcdServer` example and `Worker` docstring (#198238, #199255) ## Profiler - Fix the `toggle_collection_dynamic` example (#190369) ## Dynamo - Remove references to the obsolete `dynamic_shapes` config (#198707) - Fix the PGO config example in the dynamic shapes docs (#191027) - Document more `torch._logging.set_logs` options (#188138) ## Inductor - Document the FlexAttention `ROWS_GUARANTEED_SAFE` requirement (#194154) ## Foreach - Fix in-place foreach type stubs to return the input list (#193466) ## Release Engineering - Fix docs search ranking module stub pages above the API symbols they document and listing duplicate results (#195042) - Link the build environment variable reference from `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and fix outdated build instructions there (#193617) - Document the issue and pull request workflow in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and add a maintainer guide to the community docs (#198527) ## MPS - Note MPS lacks `float64` support (#193545) ## ROCm - Document gfx1151 SDPA layouts, hipFile GPUDirect Storage, and MI300 matmul precision issues (#190771, #195478, #190736) # Security ## Python Frontend - Fix `torch.load(weights_only=True)` exposing uninitialized pybind11-backed objects (such as DTensor placements) when a checkpoint uses the `NEWOBJ` opcode without a matching `BUILD`; such checkpoints are now rejected as corrupt or malicious (#194647) - Fix a stack buffer overflow in `torch_shm_manager` (libshm) when the Unix socket path is too long (e.g. a long `TMPDIR`); it now raises an error (#195183) - After `import torch.distributed`, `torch.load(weights_only=True)` and `get_unsafe_globals_in_checkpoint` no longer treat builtin exceptions as safe globals (a process-wide allowlist added in 2.14), and loading no longer calls overridden `append`/`extend` on allowlisted `list` subclasses. Checkpoints with pickled exceptions now need `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals`; object collectives are unchanged (#200956) # Developers ## Distributed (c10d) - Make `FakeProcessGroup` support `all_to_all_single` with any sizes and add a `simulate_uniform_ranks` option (#193985, #194545) - Fix a clang build error and add `amd_smi` as a ROCm 7.14+ build dependency (#194104, #192520) - Add the private `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.wait_tensors`, which waits on all outputs of a multi-output functional collective at once; `torch.compile` uses it for coalesced collectives and `batch_isend_irecv` (#193892) ## Profiler - Kineto source now lives in `third_party/kineto` instead of a git submodule (#198648) - Remove the ignored `profiler_metrics` and `profiler_measure_per_kernel` `_ExperimentalConfig` arguments (now a `TypeError`), and deprecate the no-op `adjust_profiler_step` option (#198262, #193042) ## FX - Fix type annotations on `Tracer(autowrap_modules=...)` and `CodeGen.process_inputs` (#195467, #188287) ## Inductor - Add `DeviceInterface` and `DeviceOpOverrides` extension points for out-of-tree accelerator backends (#190326, #190614, #192896, #193908, #190615) - Add declarative `implies` support to Inductor/Dynamo `Config` (#196663) ## Ahead-Of-Time Inductor (AOTI) - Add `DeviceOpOverrides.aten_device_type()` so backends provide their ATen device type to AOTInductor C++ codegen (#193904) ## C++ Frontend - `c10::List` iterators satisfy `std::random_access_iterator`, and `List::emplace` now constructs a `T` (#196002) ## Developer Experience - Add `spin test` to run `pytest` or `test/run_test.py` like CI (#198649) ## Build Frontend - Add an opt-in `USE_CMAKE_INSTRUMENTATION=1` build option to collect build metrics (CMake >= 4.3) (#189455) - Turn off `USE_FLASH_ATTENTION` automatically when no target CUDA architecture is sm80 or newer (#194502) - Fix the misspelled `CUDA_LIMIT_GPU_ARCHITECTURE` in CUDA architecture autodetection (#195695) - Honor `USE_MIMALLOC=OFF` on Windows and AArch64 (#199064) - Fix the FlashAttention CUDA build on Windows with MSVC in C++20 mode (#197382) ## Release Engineering - Move the CD wheel build scripts under `.ci/wheel/` (`.ci/manywheel/` to `.ci/wheel/linux/`, `.ci/macwheel/` to `.ci/wheel/mac/`, and the Windows pipeline to `.ci/wheel/windows/`) and share one `numpy` build pin (#189275) - Add a native-AOT stage to CUDA builds that exports CuTeDSL and Triton kernels ahead of time and embeds them into `libtorch_cuda`. The stage skips itself when it does not apply (for example CUDA older than 13 or no supported GPU architecture), but once it decides to export, a missing `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` (or Triton, installable with `scripts/install_triton_wheel.sh`) is a hard error; set `TORCH_NATIVE_AOT=0` to skip the stage (#194243, #196747, #196507) - Fix the CMake C and C++ compiler flag checks sharing one cache variable, so a result for one language could be reused for the other; the generated `HAS_` variables are now prefixed `HAS_C` and `HAS_CXX` (#197614) - Add a persistent `[no-ci]` PR title prefix that skips build, test and lint jobs, and make `@pytorchbot merge -i` ignore current failures across every PR in a ghstack stack (#196534, #197143) ## CUDA - Update the bundled CUTLASS to v4.8.0 and CUTLASS-Operators to v0.3.0 (#198179) ## CPU (AArch64) - Add the `AT_VEC_CUSTOM_MATH` compile definition, which hides the built-in vectorized math functions on AVX2, AVX512, NEON and SVE256 builds so that a vectorized math library other than SLEEF can be plugged in (#197419) ## MPS - Fix building with clang 16 and Apple clang 15 (#199115) - Fix building with a Metal 4 toolchain against older macOS SDKs, and deprecation warnings with the macOS 27 SDK (#196104, #197200) - `at::mps::MPSProfiler` `begin*`/`end*` methods take the `MPSStream*`; stream-less `begin*` overloads are deprecated (#192525, #193611) - Fix macOS builds failing on SDKs that lack the Metal 4 cooperative-tensor APIs (#195302) - Fix stale embedded Metal shaders in incremental macOS builds (#196202) - Fix MPS shader includes in editable installs (#195295) ## ROCm - `torch.utils.cpp_extension.ROCM_VERSION` now uses the ROCm SDK version instead of the HIP runtime version, and `collect_env` reports both (#194985, #193602) ## XPU - Build XPU with pure SYCL compilation and support Clang as the host compiler; expose `USE_SYCLTLA` and enable oneMKL sparse in the build system (#194185, #198720, #196387, #198200) - Upgrade oneDNN to v3.13 (#196712) ## Caffe2 - Fix source builds with CUDA 13.3 (#194659)

## What's Changed
* [PR] fix: external summary mode stops injecting the summary-writing rules (#4460) by @naerymdan in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4462
* [PR] feat: Codex Desktop Plugin (Git marketplace + MCP tools + version sync) | feat: Codex 桌面版插件（Git marketplace + MCP 工具 + 版本同步） by @Chrockution in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4449
* [PR] fix: restore native ACP injection across DSH and Codex by @tgazer933-boop in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/3510
* [PR] fix(#3501): explicit BILLION_CONTEXT_ATTACH outranks routed model-origin evidence in pi/omp/opencode attach probes by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/3515
* [PR] storage: position-independent row identity + historian tombstones (#4390) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4395
* [PR] #4316 Layer 3 (number directly mapped to canonical seq) PR 1/3: Fold-overwrite into real seq range | #4316 层3(编号直连正史 seq)PR 1/3:折叠覆盖写入真实 seq 区间 by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4335
* [PR] storage: seq ledger foundations — block interval bounds + ledgerSeq ref stamping (#4316 layer 3, phase 1) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4346
* [PR] feat(ci): label-driven backport carry PRs onto patch lanes (bugfix-v<latest tag>) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4503
* [PR] fix(#4506): release media refs on historian retire + budget the #3250 custom-cap slack (#4390 follow-ups) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4511
* [PR] feat: plugin-lane server-owned history — msgid pinning + transcript render endpoint | 插件车道服务端正史:msgid 钉身份 + 正史渲染端点 by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4505
* [PR] docs: document host-side retry layering product bounds (#2568 item 4) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/2569
* [PR] docs: tighten the dsh compaction-off recipe (disabled: true + all three presets) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/3294
* [PR] docs(configuration): document lowering maxContextLimit as an eager-compression lever by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4364
* [PR] docs(storage): state planIngestDelta's strict-append precondition and pin the #4182 duplicate-identity corpus by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4399
* [PR] web/stats: expose decompress usage counters to humans (#3671 direction 4) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/3684
* [PR] fix(#4227): honest compression diagnostics — cumulative shrink/postCtx over all blocks, internal-lane receipts pinned to the round's own offer by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4229
* [PR] DSH: Context tab fills the conversation view | DSH「上下文」标签页铺满会话区 by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4284
* [PR] test: golden drive refuses to run on a stale kernel dist (#3325 lesson) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/3330
* [PR] test(logger): synchronize late registration with proven delivery by @0XCocoa in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4303
* [PR] fix: clamp learned image cost to the payload's own prior (#4153) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4156
* [PR] fix: anthropic lane double-counts cached tokens on OpenAI-semantics relays (#4128) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4132
* [PR] fix: recover fold coverage after short-request deactivation under id churn (#4050) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4085
* [PR] fix: surface Node.js upgrade warning on unsupported-node storage degrade (#4444) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4451
* [PR] docs: FAQ — combining bili with a model-routing gateway (magpie) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4448
* [PR] feat(pi): fold /acp block details with Ctrl+O by @yanhuojiyusheng in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4065
* [PR] fix: redact storage diagnostics at the publish boundary by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4499
* [PR] feat: four-host msgIds wiring on the incremental lane (dsh/pi/opencode/omp) (#4491 host batch) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4523
* [PR] fix(judge): render-lane turns reconcile against the rendered baseline, not inbound bytes (#4241) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4531
* [PR] docs: restore dropped pluginLaneServerHistory seed row — unblocks docs-sync on master by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4524
* [PR] fix(ci): post carry receipts with -F so the @- stdin field is parsed by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4519
* [PR] merge: tier-1 consolidation train — 37 green PRs as one (conflicts resolved, #4294 reverted) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/4525
* [PR] feat(codex): concurrent multi-session under the same CODEX_HOME + CODEX_SQLITE_HOME shared state DB (#3203 / #2222) | [PR] feat(codex): 同一 CODEX_HOME 并发多会话 + CODEX_SQLITE_HOME 共享状态库 (#3203 / #2222) by @ranxianglei in https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/pull/3321

name: v0.41.0
body:
### Breaking Changes

- **`@agent-browser/eve` tools now come from the MCP tool catalog.** The extension exposes the CLI's MCP tools instead of 21 hand-written ones, so tool names and inputs change: `navigate` is `open`, `evaluate` is `eval`, `press_key` is `press`, `select_option` is `select`, `set_checked` is `check` and `uncheck`, `get` is `get_text`, `get_url` and the other `get_*` tools, `tabs` is the `tab_*` tools, and `wait_for` is the `wait_*` tools. The same names apply to `@agent-browser/eve/tools` overrides. The sandbox needs agent-browser 0.41, which the extension installs by default (#2241)

### New Features

- Added **`agent-browser mcp call <tool> '<json>'`** to run one MCP tool without a stdio session and print its result as JSON with the agent-browser version, for runtimes that cannot keep a process open between tool calls (#2238)
- Added **`@agent-browser/sandbox/mcp-tools.json`**, every MCP tool with its title, description, input schema, annotations and profiles, generated from the CLI and checked by a test (#2240)

### Improvements

- **`@agent-browser/eve` runs each tool as its own short-lived process**, so no `agent-browser` process outlives a tool call. The 28 `core` tools are listed to the model and the other 14 are deferred, found with `eve__search`, which keeps the listed tool context at its previous size (#2241)

### Bug Fixes

- **MCP tool arguments can no longer set global flags.** The CLI reads global flags anywhere in its arguments, so a value such as a selector or `extraArgs` entry could carry its own `--allowed-domains` and override the server or caller allowlist. Tool calls that try are now rejected (#2238)

### Contributors

- @Railly
- @lahfir

body:
## Features

# OpenWhispr 1.11.0

Teams can now share a dictionary, the assistant can follow skills you keep for recurring work, and a bunch of new models.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **📚 Shared team dictionary** — Business and Enterprise members get their team's words in dictation and meeting notes. Your own words still come first.
- **🧩 Skills** — Save instructions for recurring work in Integrations → Skills. The assistant picks a fitting skill on its own.
- **🤖 New models** — GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude 5.5 on Bedrock, Gemma 4, Qwen3.8 and more. Older models keep working if you already use them.
- **🏢 Workspace switcher** — Switch workspaces and invite people from the sidebar. Your account now lives under your avatar in the top bar.
- **⚡ Whisper GPU fallback** — Whisper checks that CUDA or Vulkan actually started and falls back to CPU if not.


## 🛠 Fixes

- The app now starts after a second account signs in on the same device.
- On macOS, slow apps get your transcript, not your old clipboard. On Windows, AltGr no longer triggers Ctrl+Alt hotkeys.
- Meeting transcripts survive recording again, uploaded audio lands in the Transcript tab, and meeting prompts show up when they should.
- Dictionary sync no longer drops words on a new device, and moved folders keep their chats.
- Linux: paste works in Omarchy agent terminals, and Hyprland configs are written safely.

Full details in the [changelog](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#1110---2026-10-29).

## 🙏 Thanks

Thanks to @greatcoat, @boseq, @Chadpiha, @IdrisGit, @hsusul, @widechaos, @etzelm, @hsearcy, @devanshc777 and @Adityakk9031, and to @tadsn3w, @hello-sebastian, @timh-86, @0xShinRai, @Hannes1909 and @graysky2 for their bug reports. 🎉

name: MinerU 4.1.0
body:
## 中文

- **主流平台与 GPU 自动加速**：默认安装支持 Windows、Linux 和 macOS 上的 CPU 运行，以及 Intel、AMD、NVIDIA 和 Apple Silicon 兼容独显或集显的推理加速。自动选择合适的 GPU 或 CPU；代表性核心推理场景的速度约为 CPU 的 **2～3 倍**。
- **统一 Tasks 异步接口**：以 `/v1/tasks` 替换旧 `/v1/uploads`、`/v1/parse/jobs` 工作流，支持文件清单、URL 输入、缓存免传、逐文件执行与结果下载，以及统一的状态查询和取消操作。详见 [Tasks 接口说明](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/blob/mineru-4.1.0-released/docs/zh/usage/tasks.md)。
- **可恢复的同步解析服务**：独立的 `file-parse-server` 提供 `/v1/file_parse`，支持单文件上传和附件返回、等待超时后查询，以及通过请求 ID 恢复已知任务。详见 [file-parse 接口说明](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/blob/mineru-4.1.0-released/docs/zh/usage/file_parse.md)。
- **硬件诊断与档位推荐**：新增 `mineru-kit hardware detect` 和 `hardware info`，帮助选择合适的服务档位，并查看设备、运行环境与校准信息。

**升级提示：** Python 支持范围调整为 **3.11–3.14**。此次包含破坏性 HTTP 接口变更，请协调升级服务端、Router、SDK 和客户端，详见 [4.1 迁移说明](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/blob/mineru-4.1.0-released/docs/zh/reference/migration_4_1.md)。

## English

- **Automatic acceleration across major platforms and GPUs:** The default installation supports CPU inference on Windows, Linux, and macOS, plus accelerated inference on compatible Intel, AMD, NVIDIA, and Apple Silicon GPUs, including integrated graphics. MinerU automatically selects suitable GPU or CPU execution; representative core inference workloads run at approximately **2–3× CPU speed**.
- **A unified asynchronous Tasks API:** `/v1/tasks` replaces the previous `/v1/uploads` and `/v1/parse/jobs` workflow, supporting file manifests, URL inputs, cached-upload reuse, per-file execution and downloads, status queries, and cancellation. See the [Tasks API reference](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/blob/mineru-4.1.0-released/docs/en/usage/tasks.md).
- **Recoverable synchronous file parsing:** The standalone `file-parse-server` provides `/v1/file_parse` for single-file uploads and attachment responses, with queries after wait timeouts and request IDs for recovering known tasks. See the [file-parse API reference](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/blob/mineru-4.1.0-released/docs/en/usage/file_parse.md).
- **Hardware diagnostics and tier recommendations:** New `mineru-kit hardware detect` and `hardware info` commands help select a suitable service tier and inspect devices, runtime versions, and calibration information.

**Upgrade note:** Supported Python versions are now **3.11–3.14**. This release includes breaking HTTP API changes; upgrade servers, Routers, SDKs, and clients together. See the [4.1 migration guide](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/blob/mineru-4.1.0-released/docs/en/reference/migration_4_1.md).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU/compare/mineru-4.0.12-released...mineru-4.1.0-released

name: v2.0.0-next.9
body:
### Features
- feat(release): one-click main path in release.yml (route job, channel next|latest, confirm_latest, npm, release commit and tag on main, GitHub release)
- feat(release): smoke --layout main (subfolder plugin, root clone marketplace) and a qwen leg that checks --agent qwen
- feat(release): commit-main.mjs, release commit and tag on main in one push, rollback as a forward commit
- feat(build): main tree writes root gemini and qwen manifests pointing into plugins/claude-code
- feat(release): plan --main --channel next|latest, version from tags and commits on main (no release branch)

### Fixes
- fix(store): writable connections run synchronous=NORMAL, a COMMIT is no fsync (D-HOOK-SYNC-1)
- fix(e2e): GP11 allows the release package.json meta keys and checks them against package.json
- fix(manifests): plugin manifests carry the v2 version and description (D-PKG-META-1)
- fix(build): v2 package.json is the source of release fields, drop v1 and unused deps
- fix(ci): ctx_batch deadline test has no wall-clock budget; heldout search p95 takes the lowest of 3 passes (D-CI-BATCH-DEADLINE-1, D-CI-PERF-2)

### Performance
- perf(hook): resolveProject computes projectKey, projectDir and dbPath on first read (D-CI-PERF-8)
